name: Li Auto Inc.

profile.description: Li Auto Inc. designs, develops, manufactures and sells premium smart electric vehicles in China. It pioneered extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs) with its L-series family SUVs and has expanded into battery-electric vehicles (MEGA MPV and i-series). Founder and CEO Li Xiang is repositioning the company as an AI company, targeting Level 4 autonomous driving by 2028 and developing humanoid robots. After 2025 deliveries fell 18.8% to 406,300 units, the company is in a model-refresh cycle led by the all-new L9 launched in Q2 2026.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (2/3): Li Auto built China's leading EREV franchise, growing revenue from RMB 8.9B in FY2020 to RMB 144.5B in FY2024, but the MEGA BEV was hit by an 11,411-unit battery-fire recall and FY2025 revenue fell to RMB 112.3B [5][6]. AI Deployment (2/2): The company ships in-house autonomous driving software to customers and says a reorganization raised model iteration from roughly every two weeks to daily [3][4]. Market Share Leadership (1/2): A major premium NEV player that has lost its sales crown, with 2025 deliveries down 18.8% [6]. Product Pipeline (2/2): The all-new L9 launched in Q2 2026, management targets L4 autonomy no later than 2028, and humanoid robots are in development [3][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of RMB 11.3B was 10.1% of revenue, well above the auto-industry norm [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Li Auto's mission of creating a 'mobile home' and happiness for families is specific and has shaped its family-SUV product line since founding [3]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes sustainability reports and reviews 20 material ESG issues with its board, but no distinctive dollar-quantified community programs were found [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Several senior autonomous-driving leaders left in late 2025, employees voiced dissatisfaction with the AI focus in January 2026, and staff were dismissed over the MEGA recall [3][6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful insider buying was found.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated on the Growth-sleeve formula. D/E of 22.3% scores 1.00 and the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 65.9% (derived from RMB 8.94B to RMB 112.3B) scores 1.00 at 2x weight [5][8]. ROE of -6.6% (2x weight) and the TTM profit margin of -4.4% score 0, revenue growth of -15.1% YoY scores 0.16, and forward P/E of 28.5 scores 0.79 [8][9]. FMP's forward PEG of 0.06 was excluded because it is distorted by the swing from TTM losses to projected profits, leaving 3.95/8 = 4.94, rounded to 5 [9]. Liquidity is ample: 2.83M ADS x $11.03 = ~$31M/day [8].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Designing and manufacturing vehicles is physical work that AI cannot replace, and Li Auto is investing heavily in becoming an AI developer itself [3][4]. In China's EV market, though, intelligent driving and in-car AI are now core purchase criteria, and analysts warn that Li Auto's AI push may be 'too shallow, and perhaps too late' against AI-native rivals [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Autonomous-driving features are bundled into vehicle prices, and no separate AI revenue is disclosed [1].

infinite_game.summary: Li Xiang is a founder-CEO willing to bet the company on a long-term AI vision, which Sinek would recognize as Courage to Lead. The cost has been internal friction, executive turnover and blame-oriented responses to quality failures, which undercut the Circle of Safety. The company's identity is in flux as it moves from family EREV maker to self-described AI company.

just_cause.analysis: The 'mobile home for families' purpose has guided Li Auto's product decisions since its 2015 founding under the same founder [3]. Leadership now frames AI and embodied intelligence as an extension of that purpose rather than a diversion, but the cause has not yet been tested across leadership transitions [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Employees openly pushed back on the CEO's AI emphasis during the January 2026 sales slump, senior autonomous-driving leaders departed and the team was dissolved into software [3]. The company publicly disciplined 14 people and terminated several employees after the MEGA fire, which signals a blame culture rather than psychological safety [6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Management describes the all-new L9 as a bid to 'regain leadership' in flagship SUVs and talks of becoming a 'leading AI company,' which is finite, ranking-oriented language [3][4]. No commentary acknowledging rivals as teachers was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Li Auto has moved from EREV-only to BEVs and is now trying to reinvent itself as an AI and robotics company [3][4]. The pivot is under way but unproven, and early BEV efforts like the MEGA stumbled [6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Li Xiang kept R&D at RMB 11.3B in FY2025 even as net income fell from RMB 8.0B to RMB 1.1B, and reaffirmed the AI and humanoid-robot strategy despite internal dissent and sliding sales [3][5]. He has also paid for a free battery replacement across 11,411 MEGA vehicles rather than minimize the recall [6].

investment_thesis: Li Auto combines a net-cash-rich balance sheet (cash of ~RMB 85/share against 65 book value per share) and a strong 5-year growth record with an aggressive bet on AI-defined vehicles and robotics, all at about 0.7x sales and 1.1x book [9]. Q2 2026 revenue rose 12% QoQ, operating margin improved from -13.0% to -9.0%, and management expects margin expansion in the second half as the new L9 mix improves [1].
thesis_continued: The near-term picture is weak. Q2 revenue fell 15% YoY, gross margin halved to 11.0%, the company lost CN¥1.7B in the quarter, and Q3 guidance of RMB 26.6B-28.0B came in below expectations [1][2]. Execution on the AI pivot, cultural repair after leadership turnover, and China's price war will determine whether Li Auto recovers its premium franchise.
key_catalysts: Margin recovery toward the 15%-20% long-term gross margin target as the all-new L9 and refreshed lineup scale in H2 2026 [1][4]
Progress toward Level 4 autonomous driving (target no later than 2028) and humanoid-robot launches validating the AI strategy [3]
Q3 2026 delivery guidance of 95,000-100,000 units marking stabilization after 2025's 18.8% decline [1][6]
key_risks: Intense Chinese EV price war and AI-native competitors eroding share; 2025 deliveries fell 18.8% [6]
Continued losses (Q2 2026 net loss of CN¥1.7B) and negative operating cash flow [2][9]
Quality and safety risk after the 11,411-unit MEGA battery-fire recall, plus talent attrition in autonomous driving [3][6]
